subject: Post-demo: least-privilege support access, log retention, and residency clarifications
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alice Morgan <alice.morgan@finsecure.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sun, 09 May 2027 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo: least-privilege support access, log retention, and residency clarifications

Hi Alice —

Thanks again for the demo today. Good conversation with your security team on the data residency and support access constraints. Per our call, I wanted to capture agreed follow-ups and a couple of clarification questions so we can move the procurement conversation forward.

Quick recap / agreed items:
- Redwood hosted offering can be scoped to run in us-west-2 for FSH’s initial region requirement.
- Support access is available via scoped, time-limited break-glass with audit logging; cross-tenant access requires explicit customer approval.
- We shared high-level log retention options (30/90/365 days) and a mapping to available audit artifacts (request traces, operator session logs, model invocations).

Clarification questions from your security team that we promised to confirm:
1) For break-glass support access, do you require MFA + just-in-time approval flow through your ticketing system (e.g., ServiceNow)?
2) Minimum RBAC granularity: do you need per-environment + per-model roles, or is per-environment sufficient?
3) Log retention: is there a mandated minimum of 365 days for all audit logs, or only for long-term billing/forensics?

Next steps I propose:
- We’ll send a short appendix that describes: break-glass workflow, exact audit artifacts we surface, and a recommended RBAC role matrix for your platform. (Ben will draft.)
- We’ll attach the SOC2 evidence map and a support-access one-pager for your security review.
- Tentatively schedule a 30-min follow-up with your SEC and Ops on Thursday to align on the RBAC matrix.

I’ve attached the two docs we said we’d share. Ben / Marissa — assigning the appendix and RBAC matrix; want to get a draft to Alice by EOD Wednesday PT.

Thanks,
Karthik

--
Karthik Iyer
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com
(415) 555-0192

Attachments:
- Redwood_Support_Access_Overview.pdf (summary of break-glass flows, MFA options, operator session capture)
- SOC2_evidence_map.xlsx (mapping of evidence artifacts to common control categories)

From: Alice Morgan <alice.morgan@finsecure.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: security@finsecure.com
Date: Mon, 10 May 2027 09:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: least-privilege support access, log retention, and residency clarifications

Thanks, Karthik — this is helpful. A couple quick answers from the FinSecure side to unblock details before Thursday: 

- Break-glass: yes, we prefer a just-in-time approval model tied to a ticket in ServiceNow. MFA is required for any elevated operator session.
- RBAC granularity: we need per-environment + per-model roles for production environments. Non-prod can be coarser.
- Log retention: our baseline requirement is 365 days for operator session logs and request traces; we can keep model-level telemetry for 90 days unless we escalate to legal/forensics.

Can you confirm whether operator sessions include keystroke-level capture or just session start/stop with command audit? We prefer the latter (no keystroke). Also please confirm whether support break-glass access will generate an auto-ticket into our ServiceNow instance (preferred) or whether it would require manual confirmation.

Alice
Director, Security Engineering
FinSecure Health
alice.morgan@finsecure.com
(617) 555-2277

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Alice Morgan <alice.morgan@finsecure.com>
Date: Tue, 11 May 2027 11:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: least-privilege support access, log retention, and residency clarifications

Karthik / Marissa — looping in draft language for the appendix below (first pass). Comments welcome; we should keep the language non-prescriptive but specific enough for procurement/security. I’ll convert to PDF and attach to the next email.

--- Draft appendix (internal) ---
1) Break-glass workflow:
   - Trigger: Customer raises a ServiceNow incident with severity and justification. ServiceNow triggers just-in-time access request to Redwood.
   - Approval: Configurable approvers (customer-defined). Redwood operator receives one-time temp credentials valid for X hours.
   - Audit: Operator session start/stop timestamp, operator identity, IP, list of commands executed (we can redact command bodies). No keystroke-level capture by default.
   - ServiceNow integration: Redwood can create an automated incident entry via our webhook/connector; confirmation is recorded both sides.

2) RBAC role matrix (summary):
   - Roles: viewer, auditor, operator, admin
   - Scope: roles can be scoped to environment (non-prod/prod) and to model namespace (per-model).
   - Example: operator-prod-modelX => can tail logs and run debug traces; cannot export raw data unless explicitly approved.

3) Log retention & artifacts:
   - Audit artifacts: request traces (headers, timestamps, user-id), operator session logs (start/stop, identity, IP, commands metadata), system-level traces (resource allocation, instance IDs).
   - Retention options: 30/90/365 days configurable per artifact type.
   - Long-term export: we can deliver encrypted exports to a customer-owned S3 for >365d retention.

Open question for Alice: do you want the default production operator session logs to be retained 365d, and model telemetry 90d (we can adjust per-deal)?

Ben
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwoodinference.com

Attachments to include in outgoing: Redwood_Support_Access_Overview.pdf (final), SOC2_evidence_map.xlsx (final)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alice Morgan <alice.morgan@finsecure.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 12 May 2027 10:23:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: least-privilege support access, log retention, and residency clarifications

Alice — appreciate the quick answers. Short responses to your two remaining items below, plus proposed next steps: 

- Operator sessions: we do NOT capture keystroke-level data by default. Our operator session logs include start/stop timestamps, operator identity, IP address, and the list of high-level commands executed (command names and metadata). If you need deeper capture we can discuss a constrained option but it will require explicit approval and narrow scope.
- ServiceNow integration: Redwood supports an automated webhook that will create a linked incident in your ServiceNow instance and return an approval token. When a break-glass request is approved via that flow it generates the operator session and logs; all artifacts are cross-referenced with the ServiceNow incident ID.

Proposed next steps:
1) Ben to publish the appendix PDF + SOC2 evidence map (attached) by EOD today.
2) Schedule the 30-min follow-up with your SEC + Ops — suggested slots: Thu 05/13 09:00 or 14:00 PT. Please confirm which works for you.
3) Draft contract addendum language (RBAC + retention) to be circulated once appendix is agreed.

If that sounds good I’ll lock the follow-up and Ben will push the attachments.

Thanks — look forward to closing this out.

Karthik
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
